recipes.name: Perfect Sesame Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - cubed

steps.text: Prepare the battered chicken: Sift flour, 2 tablespoons cornstarch, baking soda, and baking powder into a bowl. Pour in low-sodium soy sauce, sherry, 2 tablespoons water, vegetable oil, and dash sesame oil; stir until smooth. Stir in chicken until coated with the batter, then cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the sauce: Bring chicken broth, sugar, vinegar, dark soy sauce, sesame oil, chile paste, and garlic to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Dissolve 1/4 cup cornstarch into 1/2 cup water, and stir into boiling sauce. Simmer until the sauce thickens and turns clear, about 2 minutes. Reduce heat to low, and keep sauce warm.
Heat olive oil in a deep fryer or large saucepan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Carefully drop in battered chicken pieces, a few at a time, and fry until they turn golden brown and float to the top of the oil, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.
To serve, place fried chicken pieces onto a serving platter, and pour the hot sauce overtop. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds to garnish.

raw_recipe.headline: Perfect Sesame Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Tender, crispy sesame chicken in a sweet and tangy sauce that's easy to customize to make it more sweet or spicy, depending on how you like it.

review.reviewBody: To cut down on fat, I baked rather than fried this chicken, and it was still to die for! I followed all directions except when it came time to put them in the olive oil, I put them on my stoneware pan with all the marinade (which made for a nice breading) drizzled 1/4 olive oil over top, and baked at 375 for 47 minutes. I turned the chicken half way through baking. The dipping sauce thickened up just perfectly! I only used 1/2 cup of sugar and it was still plenty sweet. Thanks for a great recipe, my hubby loved it!

Pretty good recipe as is, but I tweaked it just a bit for my personal tastes. For the sauce, I cut the sugar in half, and added 2 tsps tamarind paste. Really made the sauce pop. Also for the oil temps, 375 was way to high. I cooked at 325 (candy thermometer to keep temp consistent) and it didn't burn the outer coating. Speaking of the coating - awesome! Just the right crisp, and texture.

After reading dozens of thoughtful reviews, I took into account all significant complaints and suggestions for improvement. That said, here are the adjustments made that created my favorable first experience: 

I used just under a 1/2 cup of Turbinado sugar (considering the sauce being too SWEET the most common negative review). 

Furthermore, the 2nd most recurring statement was this recipe yields exceptionally more SAUCE than is needed, but that was not an issue for me. Although, I had 1.5 pounds of chicken, I still could've used a little more sauce because I like mixing it with sticky rice. Speaking of the chicken: I used THIGHS after learning several other recipes recommend it over breast for a superior result in taste and tenderness.

Also, the chicken marinated for almost 20 hrs which leads me to the 3rd most popular complaint - the BATTER or there lack of, so I tossed it with a cup of cornstarch in a covered plastic container for a couple minutes to coat the chicken thoroughly before "deep" frying (I used 3 cups of Peanut Oil) not once, but twice. I was aiming to achieve that extra crunch; however, my chicken came out overcooked due to my zero experience in deep frying. 

Lastly, I took into consideration the potent quality of the Sesame oil, so I only used 1/2 tablespoon for the sauce and I only put 1/4 cup of cornstarch in the water but I only needed 70% of the mixture to thicken it just right. 

In conclusion, if I hadn't overcooked the chicken and if I had prepared

I used 1/4 of the sugar, half of the corn starch/water mixture that is added to the simmering sauce (the full amount turned the sauce way too thick for my taste), and a few drops of da bomb hot sauce to the simmering sauce (warning, pretty spicy). I cut the chicken into long thin strips, used a paper towel to dab them dry (similar to frying wings), then soaked them in the marinade and later air fried (400 degrees for 7-10 minutes). Served on a bed of rice, steamed broccoli on the side. I love it, will probably be cooking it multiple times a month

Listen up! :) 
My teens LOVE Chinese food, so I thought I'd give this a try, but I took a short cut... or two. 

I had (TraderJoes) frozen battered (orange) chicken pieces in freezer, and baked according to instructions while making sauce. ( I tossed the sauce that came in the bag. )
I halved recipe for sauce, bc of amount of chicken I had on hand. I also substituted brown sugar for white, and sweet chili paste for super spicy chili paste. I used white vinegar. Grating the garlic clove into the pan, and adding the ingredient list took 3 minutes. I also substituted chicken stock to mix slurry of corn starch, bc it was right there on counter. :) 
 The amount of corn starch mixture was WAY too much. 
So add slowly, about half, as it thickens you can always add more to your liking. 
I left sauce for a few minutes while getting rice ready, then tossed it with chicken in a big stainless bowl, then plopped it atop of rice.
Total time: 25 minutes.
One word: DEVOURED. 
Happy cooking

I admit I’ve made a few times & made changes. To marinate chicken- only put 1/4 tsp sesame oil- no other oil. 1 tsp Chili paste. No garlic. For Sauce- sautéed garlic in small amount butter or margarine, 1 tsp chili paste again ( very spicy!) only 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, no vinegar, 1 tbsp cornstarch dissolved in I y cold water then stirred in to hot mixture. 1 tbsp honey + 1/4 c brown sugar. I sautéed chicken in least amount oil possible ( so it stick a little to pan) added sesame seeds and 1/4 tsp sesame oil to pan. Rice and Snowpeas as sides.

My husband's first words after just a couple of bites was that this recipe was going in the rotation. I followed Emily Young's method and baked the chicken rather than frying it and then added the sauce afterward. I also used 1/2 cup sugar as others mentioned. I found this recipe to be both delicious and easy!

Definitely halve the sugar! I will even try 1/3 cup sugar next time and I'm pretty sure it will still be sweet enough. I always increase the garlic in almost every recipe I make, so I upped that to three large cloves. I might add a bit more chile sauce next time too, because it could use a bit more heat. It also seemed to lack salt, but that could be because I used low-salt soy sauce. I used chicken tenders cut into 1 inch chunks and deep fried them 3 minutes in peanut oil heated to exactly 375 degrees F. The result was crispy golden brown on the outside and moist and tender inside. Perfect.

I only made the sauce as I don't deep fry, I baked the chicken instead. I used bl/sl thighs that I baked for 20 minutes at 400 degrees, poured off the fat/juices, poured on the sauce then baked 10 minutes, turned over and baked for another 10 minutes. I used only 2 tbsps brown sugar instead of white, Sambal for the chili paste and 2 tbsps of cornstarch. The chicken was very tasty, family really enjoyed. Next time make 1.5 times sauce to have extra.
***sauce: 2 cups warm water, 2 pouches chicken Herbox, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup light soya sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp each Sambal, minced ginger and minced garlic, 1/4 tsp each pepper, garlic powder and onion powder, and 1/4 cup cornstarch. Heat in microwave at 1 minute intervals, whisk each time, then pour over chicken.

I tripled this for my family. The sauce was on point. I didn't have chile paste so I used red pepper flakes instead. I did make the chicken on a sheet pan with olive oil drizzle because we do not fry . I will make again.

This recipe is AMAZING! My changes: 1) In an iron skillet, I pan seared some broccoli with garlic, ginger, salt, pepper, and olive oil until bright green with some charred bits. 2) I tripled the garlic. 3) I quadrupled the chili paste.
awesome, i don't have to pay for my Chinese anymore, i can make it at home. So good
Simple recipe, great results. Will definitely make this again!
It was tasteless and extremely too starchy & sweet. Had to throw away sauce and start new to save dinner.
I made no changes. I usually follow a recipe the first time and then make adjustments. My family loved it as is. will make it again.
Incredibly delicious and the chicken reheats really well! Highly recommend for batch cooking!
The batter for the chicken was amazing alone the sauce was a perfect match.
I read the reviews and Added a quarter cup of sugar. followed the recipe otherwise just delicious!
I made it as written but I should have read the reviews first thing and cut the amount of sugar, it’s way too sweet as is.
